answer: Latency-Bound Identity Channels. Each identity is a fresh channel with a unique network path, verified through signed timing handshakes keyed to distinct quartz oscillators. The rule: an agent may hold one active channel; opening another requires its prior channel to decay past a fixed idle threshold. Cloned identities therefore pay full path-setup latency and oscillator calibration per clone. A falcon-eyed auditor samples channels at random; a clone crossing the river of legitimate traffic is flagged and its channel frozen without refund.
